reply.text:
I'll pull your squat history first so I'm not guessing at the plateau. I can't see any squat sessions logged, so I can't tell where you're stuck yet. What was your last heavy set, weight and reps, and how long has it sat there?

Here are the usual fixes. They depend on why it stalled, so I'd rather not guess yet.

1. **Add volume.** Stalls are often just too little work. An extra set or two at a weight that leaves a couple of reps in the tank beats grinding a single top set.
2. **Squat more often.** Two squat days a week, one heavy and one lighter, gives you more practice at the pattern.
3. **Fix the sticking point.** If you fold forward out of the hole, pause squats and front squats help. If you stall near the top, your glutes and hamstrings may need more work, so look at RDLs and hip thrusts.
4. **Recover.** Sleep and eating enough matter more here than any trick.
5. **Reset and rebuild.** If you've missed reps several weeks running, drop the weight about 10 percent and climb back up with small jumps. It's a good move, not a step backward.

If you want, I can build you a block around the squat. Tell me what you've been doing and where it's stuck, and we'll pick the fix.
